cards.headline: White has taken the ko first and neither side has a local threat, so Black needs one threat more than White: KO−, not KO+.

diagrams.caption: The tree's line. Black 7 throws in and White 8 captures it: White takes the ko first. The tree marks the leaf S[KO+].

Black has no ko threat. Black 9 plays elsewhere and White 10 connects. Black can play neither at B17 nor at D19, both suicide, so White lives. White 10 at D19 instead, capturing two stones, also lives.

Black 9 retakes after a ko threat elsewhere. If White 10 plays elsewhere, Black 11 captures three stones and White's big group is left in atari at D19 with no way out: dead. White 10 at B17 or D19 dies as well.
White 10 ataris the stone at C16, but it is no ko threat, nor is an atari at D16: Black 11 captures three stones, which gives C16 a liberty at B16, and White's big group stays in atari at D19.

text: White 8 captures Black 7, so White has taken the ko first and Black cannot retake at once. Black has no other local move, so no local threat: B17 and D19 are both suicide. With no threat, Black can only play elsewhere, and White connects and lives (Diagram 2).

After a threat elsewhere, Black retakes. Then White must retake at A19 with a threat of its own, since anything else dies (Diagram 3), and White has no local threat either (Diagram 4). So Black wins only with one threat more than White: S[KO-], besogo's 'White takes first'. S[KO+] would mean that White has to find the first threat. The site's tutorial shows the same kind of corner ko under KO−.

The analyst (high confidence), both reviewers and the solver all say KO−. Black 7 is the only move there that does not lose, and White 8 is forced, so only the sign is wrong. In the research's run on ko signs, leaves where the opponent took the ko first were marked KO− 51 times and KO+ 18 times, so no site convention backs KO+. Besogo's editor saves KO+ by default when an author marks a ko without choosing the sign, which likely explains the label.
